text:
michael: Heads up — CI started failing in our poetry/pip matrix after the lockfile regen. Failing tests mostly around tokenizers import and Starlette startup.

lucy: I saw that. Seems like new tokenizers 0.18.x pulled in a new rust wheel change; reproducible locally with py38.

greg: Are we sure it's a vuln or compat? Any CVE flagged?

michael: No CVE flagged yet. Vulnerability scanners didn't flag it. But transformers 4.34 was previously pinned to tokenizers <0.18; the regen bumped it. Treat as compat-first.

anna: Priority? We should avoid reverting main if customers rely on the regen.

sam: Proposal: 1) Pin tokenizers to 0.17.* in CI constraints to stabilize, 2) Run a quick SCA scan on the new wheel, 3) Canary deploy and run smoke tests on Dedicated.

julie: +1. Also check Starlette 0.27 -> 0.28 change — there was a middleware import rename that can break FastAPI startup.

michael: Repro steps I used:
```
poetry install --no-root --with dev
pytest tests/integration/test_http.py::test_fastapi_startup -q
```
Fails with ImportError: cannot import name 'SomeMiddleware' from 'starlette.middleware'

infra-bot: CI job #2456 failed: py38-poetry-regen (see https://ci/repo/job/2456)

sam: I'll push a quick PR adding a pip constraint file with tokenizers==0.17.2 and starlette==0.27.0 for CI. Temporary change with a clear rollback note.

lucy: Also confirm KMS integration e2e tests aren't pulling in affected libs — our kms-client wrapper shouldn't touch tokenizers, but worth a sanity run.

michael: KMS layer looks unaffected. But audit logs should capture the dependency change. @sec-ops-bot can we tag the change as 'dependency: lockfile-regen' and add an audit event?

sec-ops-bot: Created audit event AE-2025-331 for 'lockfile regen bump' with metadata: author=sam, pr=null, notes="regen bumped tokenizers & starlette, CI failures observed"

julie: For patch prioritization: since scanners show no CVE, treat as P2 (compat/regen fallout). If SCA later flags a vulnerability, we escalate to P0/P1.

anna: Plan summary: sam opens PR with constraints + CI guard; michael runs a focused SCA and shares results; lucy runs dedicated canary sanity; julie will update incident tracker if customer impact appears.

sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/1234 — pins tokenizers/starlette in a constraint file, adds a short CI job to enforce constraints.

michael: Reran canary CI with pinned constraints — green. We'll keep pins until upstream publishes a compatibility note or we validate new wheel.

lucy: One follow-up: add a lint that fails CI if a lockfile change is present without a required human approval label. Auto-bots keep slipping lock changes through.

greg: We already have a pre-merge check for unreviewed lock changes but it was bypassed by the autobump bot. I'll add a rule requiring an explicit "lockfile-review" approval from eng-security for autobumps.

sam: Also added an audit tag to the PR and marked as "deferred-upgrade" in the changelog.

michael: Closing the loop — no CVE currently, compatibility break from regen. Mitigated by CI constraints and PR 1234. Tracking: AE-2025-331 + PR 1234. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
